jobs.title: Director, Company Strategy & Operations
jobs.description:
About Us

Health is the most important thing in life, and the American healthcare system is completely broken - poor outcomes, high cost, bad patient experience. We're building a new system from the ground up.

Our mission is to improve people’s health by making it easy to live a healthy lifestyle.

Nourish is the country's largest dietitian-led metabolic health clinic. We’re an AI-native digital health system matching patients with 10,000+ Registered Dietitians, physicians, medications, lab testing, and AI agents to deliver insurance-covered care across all 50 states. Founded four years ago, we've completed millions of appointments, tripled year-over-year, and partnered with health plans covering 200M+ Americans across 250+ health systems.

In 2026 we raised a $100M Series C , bringing total funding to $215M. The round was led by  Menlo Ventures , with participation from  Thrive Capital ,  Index Ventures ,  J.P. Morgan Growth Equity Partners ,  Maverick Ventures ,  Y Combinator ,  BoxGroup ,  Atomico ,  Daybreak , and  Operator Partners .

Learn more about our Series C here: Nourish Blog , Bloomberg , Fierce Healthcare , Digital Native , The Pulse Podcast .

This is not a job for everyone. We hold an extremely high bar because we believe talent density is our biggest competitive advantage. We're looking for people who actively choose hard, ambiguous problems, who run toward unglamorous work, give and receive candid feedback, and bring relentless resilience without the ego. Our work is important, but we are not self-important. We do this because we’re solving one of the hardest problems in the world, and the problem matters. If that's you, we disproportionately reward it.

About the Role

As Director, Company Strategy & Operations, you'll own the systems that translate company strategy into execution. This role sits at the center of how Nourish operates. You'll own the company's operating system — from OKRs to executive operating cadence, business reviews, board meetings, and company communications — while leading a centralized S&O team deployed against the company's highest-impact priorities.

The scope of this role is intentionally broad and dynamic. As a generalist operator, you'll work across the business to identify and solve the company's highest-priority challenges, which will evolve based on business needs. Success in this role requires the ability to quickly build context, prioritize effectively, and bring structure and execution to ambiguous problems.

You'll report to the Head of Corporate Strategy and partner closely with the CEO and executive team. This is a true player-coach role: you'll personally lead many of the company's highest-priority initiatives while building and developing a team of exceptional generalist operators capable of solving problems across every part of the business.

This role is full-time and open to NYC-based candidates only (expectation to work in-person 3-4 days per week, with some remote flexibility). Our office is located in Gramercy.

Key Responsibilities:

- Own and evolve Nourish’s operating system: Design and run the company-wide systems and processes that drive alignment and execution, including OKRs, business reviews, All Hands, executive operating cadence, and strategic communications.

- Translate company vision and strategy into execution: Partner with the Head of Corporate Strategy and CEO to translate company priorities into clear plans, ensure teams are aligned around the highest-impact work, and create the operating mechanisms to execute.

- Lead centralized surge resourcing: Build and manage a team of exceptional generalist operators deployed against the company’s highest-priority problems. Identify where the business needs additional leverage, provide resourcing, and personally lead ambiguous cross-functional initiatives.

- Partner with leaders across the business: Serve as a strategic partner to functional leaders, helping teams solve complex problems, make better decisions, and execute more effectively.

- Partner with the executive team on company-level decisions: In partnership with Strategic Finance, support board materials, strategic planning, fundraising, capital allocation, resource prioritization, and other critical decisions that shape the direction and growth of the business.

- Strengthen and scale the Corporate Strategy team: Help develop the team’s capabilities, operating model, and ways of working to maximize leverage across the business and ensure Corporate Strategy continues to be a high-impact partner to company leaders.

We’d love to hear from you if:

- You have 6–10+ years of experience combining strategy work (e.g., investment banking, strategic finance, consulting) with direct startup execution, and have led ambiguous, cross-functional initiatives with real ownership.

- You have built and/or scaled operating systems that meaningfully improved how an organization executes.

- You’re a first-principles thinker and problem solver who thrives in ambiguity, quickly builds context, challenges assumptions, identifies better ways of operating, and translates ideas into tangible operational change.

- You’re highly analytical and data-driven , comfortable building financial models, working with metrics, and translating insights into clear decisions and prioritization.

- You combine strategic thinking with operational rigor , able to define direction while managing complex initiatives with many moving pieces and strong attention to detail.

- You’re an exceptional cross-functional partner and communicator , able to build trust across executives, clinicians, operators, product, and technical teams while driving alignment and progress.

- You're comfortable partnering closely with Strategic Finance and the executive team on strategic planning, board materials, fundraising, and resource allocation decisions

- You thrive in high-ownership, ambiguous environments , bringing strong judgment, a bias toward action, and comfort navigating complexity as you build and scale new initiatives.

- You've been responsible for someone else's growth and development , as a manager or dotted-line lead. This is a player/coach seat, and you're excited for that.

About the Role

Nourish is seeking a hands-on Engineering Manager to lead Operations Engineering. Reporting to Senior Engineering Manager , you’ll help build the technology and operating systems behind one of the largest healthcare operations in the country, supporting more than 10,000 clinicians across dietitians, physicians, and therapists.

You’ll reimagine what an AI- and technology-native healthcare operation can look like—using automation to scale unlike traditional healthcare companies and making notoriously complex workflows, including billing and claims, feel simple to patients and clinicians.

This is a full-time role. We strongly prefer candidates based in New York City or San Francisco, with exceptions for truly exceptional candidates. Check out Engineering at Nourish to learn more about our team and what we’ve already built.

Key Responsibilities

- Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team of 4–5 engineers with strong technical ownership.

- Coach engineers through regular feedback, career development, calibration, and performance management.

- Scale the team through recruiting, interviewing, hiring, and onboarding.

- Stay hands-on through architecture, pair programming, coding, code reviews, and on-call.

- Partner with product and design to write requirements, shape roadmaps, scope work, plan sprints, and deliver measurable outcomes.

- Drive thoughtful decisions around system design, code quality, observability, reliability, and scalability.

- Establish effective team rituals, including sprint planning, OKR planning and reporting, quarterly planning, and retrospectives.

- Operate with urgency and sound judgment in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.

- Set the technical direction for systems that support large-scale clinical and business operations.

- Automate manual workflows and design exception-handling systems that increase operational leverage without sacrificing accuracy or patient trust.

- Simplify billing, claims, eligibility, scheduling, and other complex healthcare workflows for patients, clinicians, and internal operators.

- Partner closely with business operations, strategy, finance, clinical, product, and analytics teams to identify bottlenecks and measure business impact.

- Build reliable, auditable systems that can safely scale through rapid growth and regulatory complexity.

We’d Love to Hear from You If You:

- Have 6+ years of professional software engineering experience with modern full-stack technologies and 2+ years of hands-on engineering management experience .

- Have hired engineers and managed performance, promotions, and career development.

- Remain technical enough to pair program with your team and contribute directly when needed.

- Bring exceptional product judgment: you can write a PRD, critique or mock a design, size an opportunity, and make progress without waiting on a PM.

- Are highly proficient with React, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL , or similar modern stacks.

- Have shipped and owned production systems in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.

- Balance people leadership with technical depth, delivery focus, and clear communication.

- Are energized by Nourish’s mission to improve people’s health by making it easy to eat well.

Nice to Have:

- Backend and workflow-platform experience.

- Automation and AI-enabled operations.

- Healthcare billing, claims, or eligibility.

- Internal tools.

- Regulated systems.

- Experience designing for reliability, audibility, and complex edge cases.

About Us

Nourish is on a mission to improve people’s health by making it easy to eat well. Nutrition-related chronic disease is the largest and most overlooked crisis in the world, and food can be medicine. We’re building an AI-native, patient-friendly healthcare system centered on nutrition—live in all 50 states with thousands of dietitians and hundreds of thousands of patients on the platform.

We’ve partnered with national health insurers and provider groups, raised substantial funding from top-tier investors, and are rapidly scaling our teams to build technology that transforms how people engage with their health.

In 2026 we raised a $100M Series C , bringing total funding to $215M. The round was led by  Menlo Ventures , with participation from  Thrive Capital ,  Index Ventures ,  J.P. Morgan Growth Equity Partners ,  Maverick Ventures ,  Y Combinator ,  BoxGroup ,  Atomico ,  Daybreak , and  Operator Partners .

Learn more about our Series C here: Nourish Blog , Bloomberg , Fierce Healthcare , Digital Native , The Pulse Podcast .

This is not a job for everyone. We hold an extremely high bar because we believe talent density is our biggest competitive advantage. We're looking for people who actively choose hard, ambiguous problems, who run toward unglamorous work, give and receive candid feedback, and bring relentless resilience without the ego. Our work is important, but we are not self-important. We do this because we’re solving one of the hardest problems in the world, and the problem matters. If that's you, we disproportionately reward it.

About the Role

Nourish is seeking a hands-on Engineering Manager to lead Provider Supply. Reporting to Sarah J, you’ll own the team responsible for ensuring Nourish has the provider capacity to meet growing patient demand — and that providers can build predictable, rewarding careers on the platform.

Your team owns technology across the provider journey, from application and onboarding through scheduling, productivity, earnings, and retention. You’ll grow provider supply through two primary levers: helping existing providers operate at their full potential and creating a seamless, high-converting path for new providers to join and activate on Nourish.

This team is tackling a foundational challenge for Nourish: scaling our provider network to serve patients across the country. First, we’re rebuilding the scheduling and capacity system so providers can set achievable caseload goals, trust Nourish to fill their calendars, and earn predictably. Second, we’re transforming application through activation from a human-heavy recruiting process into a thoughtful, product-led experience — with data and automation handling repetitive work while people step in at the moments where they have the greatest impact on supporting providers in their onboarding at Nourish.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who enjoys developing engineers, shaping products, remaining close to architecture and implementation, and the details of marketplace dynamics. You’ll work closely with provider recruiting, onboarding, provider strategy, product, design, data, and finance to build systems that balance patient access, provider experience, and business performance.

This is a full-time role. We strongly prefer candidates based in New York City or San Francisco, with exceptions for truly exceptional candidates. Check out Engineering at Nourish to learn more about our team and what we’ve already built.

Key Responsibilities

- Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team of 4–6 engineers with strong technical ownership.

- Coach engineers through regular feedback, career development, calibration, and performance management.

- Scale the team through recruiting, interviewing, hiring, and onboarding.

- Stay hands-on through architecture, pair programming, coding, code reviews, and on-call.

- Partner with product and design to write requirements, shape roadmaps, scope work, plan sprints, and deliver measurable outcomes.

- Drive thoughtful decisions around system design, code quality, observability, reliability, and scalability.

- Establish effective team rituals, including sprint planning, OKR planning and reporting, quarterly planning, and retrospectives.

- Operate with urgency and sound judgment in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.

- Set the technical and product direction for Nourish’s provider supply platform.

- Build scheduling and capacity systems that help providers set achievable caseload goals, manage their availability, fill open appointments, and earn predictably.

- Improve the provider application-to-activation funnel through experimentation, automation, lifecycle-based referrals, and thoughtfully designed recruiting and onboarding experiences.

- Create human-in-the-loop systems that automate repetitive operational work and direct recruiting and operations teams toward the highest-value interventions.

- Build the data foundations needed to understand provider capacity, forecast supply, measure funnel conversion, and make effective marketplace decisions.

- Connect improvements in provider growth and productivity to patient access, provider retention, operational efficiency, and Nourish’s ability to scale.

- Partner closely with provider recruiting, onboarding, strategy, operations, product, design, data, finance, and clinical leadership.

We’d Love to Hear from You If You:

- Have 6+ years of professional software engineering experience with modern full-stack technologies and 2+ years of hands-on engineering management experience .

- Have hired engineers and managed performance, promotions, and career development.

- Remain technical enough to pair program with your team and contribute directly when needed.

- Bring exceptional product judgment: you can write a PRD, critique or mock a design, size an opportunity, and make progress without waiting on a PM.

- Are highly proficient with React, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL , or similar modern stacks.

- Have shipped and owned production systems in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.

- Are comfortable using data and experimentation to improve complex funnels, workflows, or marketplace systems.

- Balance people leadership with technical depth, delivery focus, and clear communication.

- Are energized by Nourish’s mission to improve people’s health by making it easy to eat well.

Nice To Have:

- Backend and workflow-platform experience

- Automation and AI-enabled operations

- Healthcare billing, claims, or eligibility

- Internal tools

- Regulated systems

- Experience designing for reliability, auditability, and complex edge cases.

Learn more about our Series C: Nourish Blog , Bloomberg , Fierce Healthcare , Digital Native , and The Pulse Podcast .

This is not a job for everyone. We hold an extremely high bar because we believe talent density is our biggest competitive advantage. We’re looking for people who actively choose hard, ambiguous problems, who run toward unglamorous work, give and receive candid feedback, and bring relentless resilience without the ego. Our work is important, but we are not self-important. We do this because we’re solving one of the hardest problems in the world, and the problem matters. If that’s you, we disproportionately reward it.

About the Role

We are hiring an Executive Assistant, Tech (Executive Operations Manager, Tech) to report to our Executive Operations Manager and serve as a trusted operating partner to our CTO and department heads across Engineering, Product, Design, and Analytics. The role will be most deeply focused on the CTO and VP Engineering, while providing ongoing, dependable support to each EPDA leader.

This role sits at the intersection of executive partnership and tech operations. You will maintain active support relationships with all EPDA department heads, understand what each leader needs, and allocate your time transparently as priorities shift. You will protect leadership time, keep important decisions and follow-ups moving, and build lightweight systems that help EPDA operate as one team. On any given week, that may mean redesigning a leader’s calendar around the decisions that matter, preparing an OKR or all-hands update, helping negotiate a software renewal, coordinating an EPDA offsite, or driving a security initiative across several teams.

This is a hands-on role for someone who is equally comfortable with high-stakes executive support and operational ownership. You will not just schedule meetings; you will understand why they matter, make thoughtful tradeoffs, prepare the right context, and ensure decisions turn into action.

Location and in-office expectations: In-office role in NYC. Occasional travel is expected for offsites and company events.

Key Responsibilities:

- Provide ongoing calendar, meeting, travel, preparation, and administrative support to every EPDA department head and the CTO, with the deepest and most proactive coverage for the CTO and VP Engineering; maintain a clear system for balancing requests and communicating tradeoffs across leaders.

- Serve as a go-to operating partner for EPDA leadership by preparing agendas, briefs, presentations, and decision materials and tracking commitments through completion.

- Run and improve key EPDA operating cadences, including leadership meetings, planning cycles, OKR reporting, all-hands preparation, and communications about AI use and internal efficiency.

- Manage visibility into technology vendor spend and utilization; support procurement, renewals, budgeting, and contract negotiations in partnership with Finance, Legal, Security, and functional owners.

- Project-manage cross-cutting initiatives such as security, privacy, compliance, and audit-readiness work by establishing clear owners, milestones, dependencies, risks, and escalation paths.

- Plan and coordinate EPDA offsites, leadership sessions, team events, and employer-brand initiatives that strengthen how the organization works and how candidates understand the team.

- Build strong relationships across Engineering, Product, Design, Analytics, People, Finance, Legal, Security, IT, and executive operations; identify gaps in information flow and fix them.

- Use AI, automation, and modern productivity tools to reduce repetitive work, improve reporting, and make the organization more effective without compromising judgment, privacy, or quality.

We’d love to hear from you if:

- You have 5+ years of experience in executive operations, executive business partnership, business operations, technical program management, or a similarly high-trust role in a fast-growing technology company.

- You have directly and concurrently supported multiple VP- or C-level leaders across different functions and are excellent at complex calendar management, meeting preparation, travel, executive follow-through, and transparently balancing competing leadership needs.

- You have operated across multiple technical or product functions and can build credibility with Engineering, Product, Design, Analytics, and business partners.

- You have managed budgets or vendor spend and have supported procurement, renewals, contract negotiations, or vendor performance reviews.

- You have driven ambiguous cross-functional work to completion, ideally involving security, compliance, privacy, risk, or another initiative where several teams owned dependencies.

- You communicate exceptionally well in writing and verbally and can turn incomplete inputs into clear briefs, OKR reports, presentations, and company updates.

- You have excellent judgment, discretion, and attention to detail and can decide when to act, when to ask, and when to escalate.

- You are energized by both strategic and unglamorous work, stay calm when priorities shift, and take pride in making the people and teams around you more effective.

- You are fluent with tools such as Google Workspace, Slack, Notion, spreadsheets, presentation software, and modern AI tools, and you use them thoughtfully.

Our mission is to improve people’s health by making it easy to live a healthy lifestyle.

Nourish is the country's largest dietitian-led metabolic health clinic. We’re an AI-native digital health system matching patients with 10,000+ Registered Dietitians, physicians, medications, lab testing, and AI agents to deliver insurance-covered care across all 50 states. Founded four years ago, we've completed millions of appointments, tripled year-over-year, and partnered with health plans covering 200M+ Americans across 250+ health systems.

In 2026 we raised a $100M Series C , bringing total funding to $215M. The round was led by  Menlo Ventures , with participation from  Thrive Capital ,  Index Ventures ,  J.P. Morgan Growth Equity Partners ,  Maverick Ventures ,  Y Combinator ,  BoxGroup ,  Atomico ,  Daybreak , and  Operator Partners .

Learn more about our Series C here: Nourish Blog , Bloomberg , Fierce Healthcare , Digital Native , The Pulse Podcast .

This is not a job for everyone. We hold an extremely high bar because we believe talent density is our biggest competitive advantage. We're looking for people who actively choose hard, ambiguous problems, who run toward unglamorous work, give and receive candid feedback, and bring relentless resilience without the ego. Our work is important, but we are not self-important. We do this because we’re solving one of the hardest problems in the world, and the problem matters. If that's you, we disproportionately reward it.

About the Role

As the Head of People Strategy & Ops, you will report into our VP of Operations & People and lead the People Strategy & Operations function, while also partnering closely with our Executive, Finance, IT, Clinical Strategy, Sales, and Engineering teams. You will play a pivotal role in shaping the strategy and execution of Nourish’s People function, and partner closely with the executive team and department heads to uphold Nourish’s high talent bar, develop & retain our team members, and drive performance across the company as we scale. We have a high-performance, ambitious, and fun culture, and you will be in charge of bolstering this and increasing our talent density as we scale.

This role is full-time and open to NYC-based candidates only (expectation to work in-person ~3 days per week, with some additional remote flexibility). Our office is located in Gramercy.

Key Responsibilities:

- Directly manage the People Strategy & Operations function, driving best-in-class execution + speed. Build the team as we scale, owning org design, planning, tech stack, hiring, and critical metrics for your function

- Drive strategy for the People function, including projects related to talent density, employee upskilling, manager enablement, employee retention, performance management, and culture. Drive creation of the strategic roadmap and execution on strategic projects via yourself and your team

- Build the operating system required to scale ; design the processes, tools, and decision-making cadences that help the People team and cross-functional teams sharpen performance and drive results

- Own all People Operations processes and systems ; continually work to optimize the system and drive efficiency gains via automation, tech, and process redesign. Own the People tech stack, budget & vendor relationships

- Be a trusted partner to the executive team and department heads, helping our leaders drive performance of their teams and acting as the voice of the people (upwards) and voice of the people team (outwards)

We’d love to hear from you if:

- You have 7–12+ years of experience , with a mix of strategy work (e.g., management consulting, business operations, financial services) and start-up experience; direct People and Talent-related experience preferred but not required

- You have strong people instincts and communication skills , with the ability to influence Director, VP, and C-suite stakeholders, and craft the Nourish culture as we scale

- You’re a strategic thinker who uses data and first principles to solve problems , and you aren’t afraid to do things the unconventional way. You’re open to challenging mainstream thinking if it doesn’t work for Nourish

- You’re operationally excellent ; you’re able to manage a high volume of moving pieces and competing priorities with strong attention to detail and organization skills, while still maintaining momentum and clarity in a fast-paced environment

- You’re highly collaborative and cross-functional, able to work effectively across departments to advance towards goals

- You’re energized by 0→1 and 1→10 work , and enjoy stepping into undefined spaces to build structure, momentum, and clarity where none exists

About the Role

We're building a new growth function at Nourish focused on one of the biggest opportunities in our business: helping more patients successfully engage with and return to care.

As an early member of the team, you'll own some of our highest-priority patient retention problems from 0→1 — identifying where patients are falling out of care, sizing the biggest opportunities, developing the strategy to address them, and driving solutions that measurably improve conversion, retention, and reactivation.

This is a strategic, analytical role at the intersection of strategy & operations, data, product, and lifecycle marketing. You'll start with ambiguous business problems, use data and patient insights to determine where we should focus, and then work cross-functionally to turn those opportunities into outcomes.

This is not a role where you'll inherit a mature program and optimize campaigns. You'll help determine what we should build, why it matters, and how we'll know it's working — and then own the work through execution, experimentation, and cross-functional influence.

You'll report to the Head of Lifecycle Marketing . This is a full-time role, with a preference for candidates based in NYC or SF (expectation of working from our office 3–4 days per week).

Key Responsibilities:

- Identify and size the biggest opportunities across the patient journey, using quantitative and qualitative data to understand where we're losing patients and where we can drive the most impact on retention and LTV.

- Own the strategy for high-priority retention problems , translating ambiguous business questions into clear hypotheses, roadmaps, and measurable goals.

- Drive 0→1 initiatives from insight to impact — define the problem, develop the approach, align cross-functional partners, and own execution through launch, measurement, and iteration.

- Own the metrics and experimentation roadmap for your area, turning data and experiments into clear insights on what's working and where we should invest.

- Design and scale campaigns across email, SMS, push, and product touch points — building segmentation strategy, personalization frameworks, and journey architecture.

- Partner with Product, Data, and Engineering to turn strategic opportunities into product experiences and scalable lifecycle capabilities.

We’d Love to Hear From You If You:

- You have 3–7 years of experience in strategy, consulting, product, growth, lifecycle marketing, or another high-impact role where you've owned ambiguous business problems and driven measurable outcomes.

- You're data-fluent and experimentation-rigorous, and can drive analysis from insight to action. Your strategy and decision making is rooted in data.

- You're a 0-to-1 builder who has launched programs from scratch. You’re a self-starter who doesn’t wait for direction: you identify the highest-leverage work, define the plan, and drive it through ambiguity.

- You are deeply impact-oriented.  You prioritize based on business outcomes, not activity, and have a track record of materially moving core metrics.

- You’re comfortable in fast-moving environments; you can juggle multiple priorities, adapt quickly when things shift, and thrive in hyper-growth.

- You can work well cross-functionally, building trust and alignment with different teams in a low-ego way.

- Nice to haves :

- Experience in lifecycle marketing (including hands on ESP expertise, such as customer.io , braze, iterable)

- Experience at fast-growing tech or healthcare startup

- People leadership or strong coaching skills

- Fluency with modern mar-tech stacks and engineering partnerships

You'll be trusted to lead critical cross-functional initiatives and solve problems you've never faced before.

This person will report into our CFO or Senior Strategic Finance Lead and work closely with founders and VPs across every team in the organization.

This role is full-time and open to NYC-based candidates only (expectation to work in-person 3-4 days per week, with some remote flexibility). Our office is located in Gramercy.

- Support high-importance ad hoc work, including board meetings, capital raises, and M&A

- Communicate findings and recommendations in a clear, structured way to leadership and cross-functional partners

- Proactively identify operating gaps and lead end-to-end efforts to close them
